expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (no files created or changed)
The reply identifies path traversal via the file parameter (e.g. ../ or an absolute path makes os.path.join escape UPLOADS)
expectations.evidence: The reply says "`?file=../../../etc/passwd`: `os.path.join` doesn't resolve `..`, so the path escapes the uploads folder" and "`?file=/etc/passwd`: when the second argument is an absolute path, `os.path.join` throws away `UPLOADS` entirely."

expectations.text: The reply names that any logged-in user can read files outside uploads, including other users' files, as the affected boundary
expectations.evidence: The reply names the intended limit ("downloads should be limited to `/srv/app/uploads`") and the result ("an attacker can read any file the server process can read... and every user's uploads"); it also cites the comment saying users may download only "files *they uploaded*". It describes the attack
